outcome: Give farm operations director / food quality head a governed method to improve grading consistency and false reject rate using camera images, grading examples and reject labels, with final decisions…
overview: Commodity Grade Sorting by Vision addresses inspection evidence is collected unevenly, causing missed defects and inconsistent first-pass decisions in agriculture and food production operations. The first proof of value uses camera images, grading examples and reject labels. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is grading consistency and false reject rate, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.
kpi: grading consistency and false reject rate

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: camera images, grading examples and reject labels; define grading consistency and false reject rate and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Farm Operations Director / Food Quality Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including blind review of representative images across operating conditions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
